name: workflowers-events-to-scw-busy

deploy.description: One half of the two-way calendar-blocking pair (with scw-events-to-workflowers-block; gcal-block-sweep is the shared horizon backstop). Mirrors every timed, busy, non-declined event on the dennis@work.flowers Google Calendar onto dchiuten@securecodewarrior.com as a PRIVATE, BARE 'Busy' block — no title, description, location or attendees leak into the SCW workspace. Keyed through the GCal Sync Map table so updates move the block and cancellations delete it. Refuses to create a mirror for an occurrence starting more than 30 days out; the sweep fills those in as they approach. Replaces Notion Calendar's built-in event blocking, which SCW IT cut off on 2026-08-28.

trigger.authentication_note: work.flowers Google Calendar connection ('Google Calendar dennis@work.flowers') — the calendar being READ. Same id gcal-event-updated-to-meeting-note carries on its trigger; that Zap and this one both poll dennis@work.flowers and coexist fine. The SCW credential is a --connections alias because the workflow writes there.
trigger.trigger_note: Polling trigger, fires on create AND update. Historical: with expand_recurring: true (until 2026-10-31) Zapier silently dropped cancelled tombstones (proven 2026-08-31 — 0 cancelled in 100 runs here vs 13/100 on the meeting-note Zap, whose only trigger difference is expand_recurring: false; the deleted 9am work.flowers event of 2026-08-31 left its SCW Busy block standing). Deletion propagation lives in workflowers-cancellations-to-scw-unblock (event_cancelled). The cancel branch in this workflow is kept as a belt. With expand_recurring: false cancellations may arrive here too (the meeting-note Zap saw them); the cancel branch handles them idempotently alongside the cancellations Zap.
trigger.params_note: expand_recurring: false since 2026-10-31. With it true, every edit to a recurring series re-delivered every expanded occurrence years ahead once Zapier fixed W6ZE93-VMEWP (one daily-standup edit = thousands of runs), and on 2026-10-30 those bursts exhausted the account's daily compute-spend limit, so every Zap in the account was refused until 00:00 UTC. Now a series edit arrives as ONE run carrying the series master (`recurrence` set, no `recurringEventId`); the workflow fetches only that series' occurrences inside the 30-day horizon (capped at 2026-12-31, the end of the SCW engagement) with one Google events.instances call through the `gcal_wf` alias, and mirrors each. One-off events and individually edited occurrences still arrive one by one, keyed by occurrence id (verified on gcal-event-updated-to-meeting-note, which ran expand_recurring: false).

connections_note: gcal_scw is the SCW Google Calendar connection 'dchiuten@securecodewarrior.com' (created 2026-08-28) — the DESTINATION this workflow creates/moves/deletes bare Busy blocks on. `gcal_wf` (dennis@work.flowers) is read-only here: it is the same credential as the trigger, bound as an alias since 2026-10-31 so mirrorSeries can call Google's events.instances for a series master.

tables.01M13QPJ5GRJV33096MBNSN1Q5: GCal Sync Map — source occurrence id -> mirror event id, both directions. SHARED with scw-events-to-workflowers-block and gcal-block-sweep: loop guard, update/delete target map, change detector. Columns: Source Event ID (f1), Mirror Event ID (f2), Direction (f3), Status (f4), Start (f5), End (f6), Summary (f7 — the SOURCE title, for debugging; the mirror itself is always 'Busy'), Source Updated (f8).

description: Mirror work.flowers calendar events onto the SCW calendar as private bare 'Busy' blocks — times only, no details. Creates, moves and deletes the block in step with the source.
